newsitem.title: CANADA: U.S. not to limit Canada grain - Canada spokesman.
newsitem.headline: U.S. not to limit Canada grain - Canada spokesman.

text.p: U.S. agriculture officials agreed on Friday in a meeting with their Canadian counterparts that the United States would not limit imports of Canadian grain, Canadian trade spokesman Charles Larabie said.

"There are currently no restrictions on the exports of Canadian wheat and barley to the U.S., and the U.S. will not introduce any measure to limit Canada's access to its grain market," he told Reuters.
"This was agreed upon between Canadian and U.S. officials who met in Ottawa today."
"They discussed the whole range of issues related to wheat and barley trade, and relevant market factors, and our contention all along has been this has been market-driven," Larabie said.
"We're not there to take advantage in a negative way of any situation in the U.S. market. We're there to take advantage of legitimate market opportunities."
He added: "We've been saying all along that we will not put a cap on our grain exports and I think they've understood our message."
The officials met for one day.
Canadian agriculture spokesman Mike Gifford said the Americans expressed their grain producers' concern over Canadian grain exports.

"We in turn reiterated that Canada will not agree to any limitation on Canadian grain exports, and that basically U.S. imports of wheat from Canada and barley from Canada reflected market demand," he said after the meeting.

"As far as we're concerned, the border is open and we would expect the United States to continue to honor its WTO (World Trade Organization) and NAFTA (North American Free Trade Agreement) commitments."

Grain export levels between the two neighbors have been a recurring irritant, punctuated periodically by calls from the United States for an export cap and suggestions that Canada is dumping grain in the U.S. market.

Canada's Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale had made it clear that Canada had no interest in limiting grain exports and pointed out that three U.S. investigations into Canadian trade flows in grain had failed to find any evidence of dumping.
Canadian Grain Commission statistics on April 17 showed Canada had exported 1,400,100 tonnes of wheat, durum wheat and barley to its southern neighbour between August 1 and April 17.

The U.S. government was under pressure from grain farmers in North Dakota to cap Canadian grain exports to the United States at 1.5 million tonnes -- the level set for wheat and durum in a 1994 agreement.
That agreement followed on the heels of record export levels of Canadian wheat to the United States in the 1993/94 crop year after severe flooding of the Mississippi River cut U.S. crop output.
The deal lapsed on September 12, 1995, to comply with World Trade Organization and North American Free Trade Agreement rules.
